pool.text: First Europeans arrived at Lake Maracaibo, marking initial contact with the region
Nikolaus Federmann relocated the settlement population to Santa Marta
Captain Alonso Pacheco attempted to settle Maracaibo but faced indigenous attacks
Captain Pedro Maldonado permanently re‑founded the city as Nueva Zamora
Dutch corsair Henrik de Gerard plundered Maracaibo
British pirate William Jackson attacked the city
French pirate François l'Olonnais sacked Maracaibo and Gibraltar
Henry Morgan raided Maracaibo before moving on to Gibraltar
French privateer Michel de Grammont attacked Maracaibo with six ships
Overthrow of Pérez Jiménez led to democratic administration approving new bridge project
Prestressed concrete bridge opened, linking Maracaibo with Zulia’s eastern shore
Super‑tanker Esso Maracaibo collided with bridge pier, collapsing 259 m roadway section
Diocese of Maracaibo established on 23 July
Maracaibo Diocese elevated to archdiocese by Pope Paul VI
Pope John Paul II visited Maracaibo
San Francisco municipality created as second of Maracaibo’s two municipalities
Archbishop Ubaldo Ramón Santana Sequera began leading the archdiocese
Widespread poverty and blackouts sparked violence and looting across the city
COVID‑19 pandemic overwhelmed Maracaibo University Hospital
Local solar‑energy pilot aims to install panels on 400 homes and 100 apartments
